summary: Independently verified the restoration of /app/scripts/heal_bifurcated_domains.js (BifurcationHealCron 'Cannot find module' boot error fix). All 5 requested checks PASS: (1) node --check syntax OK; (2) require() smoke-load exports runHealSweep + detectCategory (+ inspectDomain) as functions, prints OK, exit 0; (3) test_heal_bifurcated_domains_categorize.js -> 'All 14 categorize tests passed', exit 0; (4) test_bifurcation_heal_cron.js -> 'Result: 18 passed, 0 failed', exit 0 (the intentional mocked-throw stack trace appeared in section F as documented); (5) after `sudo supervisorctl restart nodejs` + 12s, nodejs RUNNING, GET http://127.0.0.1:5000/api/health -> HTTP 200 {status: healthy, database: connected}, and `tail -n 300 /var/log/supervisor/nodejs.*.log` contains NO 'Cannot find module' and NO '[BifurcationHealCron] init error' — instead the success line '[BifurcationHealCron] Scheduled — daily at 03:30 UTC (apply=A,B,D)'. Additionally confirmed `git diff bffe1653^ -- scripts/heal_bifurcated_domains.js` is EMPTY, i.e. the restored 554-line file is byte-identical to the last-good parent-commit version (staged as 'A'). SAFETY HONORED: the '/admin/bifurcation-heal/run' route was NOT invoked, and the Telegram webhook was NOT driven, so no live prod Mongo / OpenProvider / Cloudflare mutation occurred.

minor.issue: PRE-EXISTING & UNRELATED to this fix: repeated '[PhoneMonitor] Error checking number +18883304418: Request failed with status code 401' in nodejs.err.log — dev-pod Twilio/Telnyx credential 401s. Not caused by the heal-script restoration; noted only so it is not mistaken for a regression.

action_items: No fix required for this iteration — the restoration is verified correct in this pod.

REMAINING (out of scope, but required for the production fix to take effect): scripts/heal_bifurcated_domains.js is currently only STAGED in git (status 'A'). It must be committed + pushed to GitHub so Railway redeploys; until then production will still log '[BifurcationHealCron] init error (non-fatal): Cannot find module'.
critical_code_review_comments: GET /admin/bifurcation-heal/run is a state-MUTATING operation exposed over HTTP GET (when ?apply is supplied it writes to Mongo and calls OpenProvider/Cloudflare). It is auth-gated by a SESSION_SECRET prefix in a query param and defaults to dry-run, which is reasonable, but GET + secret-in-query-string is risky (leaks into access logs/referrers and is replayable/prefetchable). Recommend converting the applying path to POST with the key in a header.

The heal cron init in js/_index.js is correctly wrapped in try/catch and logs non-fatally, so a missing module degrades gracefully rather than crashing the bot — good. However the catch only logs at info level, which is exactly why this regression went unnoticed; consider surfacing init failures to the admin Telegram chat like runOnce() already does.
js/_index.js is ~44,600+ lines — pre-existing but severe maintainability risk; route/cron registration blocks like this one should be extracted into modules.
scripts/heal_bifurcated_domains.js (554 lines) is under the 700-line threshold and exports a clean surface (runHealSweep/detectCategory/inspectDomain); no issues found in the restored file.
seed_data_creation: None. No data created or mutated; all tests use in-process mocks/fakes.
test_credentials: None required for this verification (no auth flows exercised). /app/memory/test_credentials.md not needed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Verification scope was strictly: node --check, require smoke-load, 2 node unit test files (14 + 18 assertions), supervisor nodejs restart + boot-log grep + /api/health. DO NOT call GET/POST /admin/bifurcation-heal/run and DO NOT drive the Telegram webhook — both hit the SHARED LIVE production MongoDB and can mutate real domain records at OpenProvider/Cloudflare. The restored file is byte-identical to bffe1653^ (git diff empty) and is staged-but-uncommitted; if a future run sees the 'Cannot find module' error again, first check `git status scripts/heal_bifurcated_domains.js`.
rca_of_the_issue: ROOT CAUSE: commit bffe1653 deleted scripts/heal_bifurcated_domains.js while js/bifurcation-heal-cron.js:23 still did `require('/app/scripts/heal_bifurcated_domains')`. Because the init call in js/_index.js:~44585 is wrapped in try/catch, the MODULE_NOT_FOUND was swallowed into the non-fatal log line '[BifurcationHealCron] init error (non-fatal): Cannot find module ...' — the bot booted fine but the daily 03:30 UTC domain-bifurcation heal sweep silently never scheduled, so Category A/B/D divergences would accumulate unrepaired. FIX VERIFIED: `git checkout bffe1653^ -- scripts/heal_bifurcated_domains.js` restored the exact 554-line last-good file (diff vs bffe1653^ is empty). REPRODUCTION/CONFIRMATION: restarted nodejs under supervisor; the boot log now emits '[BifurcationHealCron] Scheduled — daily at 03:30 UTC (apply=A,B,D)' with zero occurrences of 'Cannot find module' or 'init error' in the last 300 log lines, and /api/health returns healthy with database connected. MITIGATION suggestion: add a CI guard that resolves every absolute `require('/app/...')` path at build time so a deleted-but-still-required module fails the build instead of degrading silently.
